 Free childcare aims to make voting easier for Colorado Springs parents 
 By Nicole Ashley Published : Oct. 21, 2026 at 10:00 AM MDT Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google COLORADO SPRINGS, Colo. (KKTV) - With in-person voting underway across El Paso County, a Colorado Springs childcare center is offering free care for parents who may need extra time to cast their ballot.
 Unique Play Place is offering free childcare on Oct. 29 to give parents time to review their ballot and vote.
 The center’s director and owner, Whisper Mondragon, said the goal is to help families who may not otherwise have the time or resources to step away from work or parenting responsibilities.
 “Need that opportunity that may otherwise not have that resource to go and have that time to cast that vote or just that time to kind of read through the ballot and all the initiatives because there is so much information on those ballots,” Mondragon said.
 The free childcare is available for children from six weeks through 12 years old. Parents can reserve up to an hour and a half of care but must sign up in advance through a Google form.
 Mondragon said the idea came from seeing how difficult it can be for parents to carve out time for important tasks, particularly for single parents, working families, and parents who are primary caregivers.
 “Whether it’s single parents who may just not have a moment to kind of go out between work schedules or parents that may even be at home at this time and not in the workforce and just need that moment to kind of say, OK, I need to focus on the task at hand,” Mondragon said.
 The effort comes as in-person voting is already underway across El Paso County. Six voter service and polling centers are open this week from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.
 At those locations, voters can cast a ballot in person, register to vote, update their voter registration or receive a replacement ballot. Voters who already received a ballot in the mail can still choose to vote in person instead.
 Mondragon said the childcare center’s broader goal is to make childcare more affordable and flexible while allowing families to participate in decisions that affect their communities.
 “We’re super excited to be offering this resource. We want to get it out to as many families as possible so they can utilize this,” Mondragon said.
 The free childcare on Oct. 29 is available by reservation only, so families will need to register ahead of time. To register, click here .
